blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Open sort menu traps keyboard focus: Tab is swallowed and Escape does nothing) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Keyboard users (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, 2.1.1 Keyboard). Once the menu opens, focus moves into it (line 12); pressing Tab or Shift+Tab is prevented and only cycles focus among the four items, and Escape has no handler, so a keyboard user cannot leave the menu or move on to the product list without picking an option. Follow the APG menu button pattern: handle Escape to close the menu and return focus to the "Sort" button, and on Tab let the default focus move happen while closing the menu (do not call preventDefault). Keep ArrowDown/ArrowUp for moving between items. A native <select> would avoid the whole issue.
findings.title: Open sort menu traps keyboard focus: Tab is swallowed and Escape does nothing

findings.evidence: <button ref={button} type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
findings.recommendation: Screen reader users (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value). aria-expanded is hard-coded to "false", so when the user activates the "Sort" button and the menu opens, the button still announces "collapsed"; the state never matches the actual behavior. Bind it to the state: aria-expanded={open}.
findings.title: Menu button always announces aria-expanded="false"
